title: Band-Pass Filter - Band 26 (850 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Takeshi Yamamoto

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Band-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 26 (850 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 1080.1 MHz and bandwidth of 211.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the IoT Narrowband Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Band-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 26 (850 MHz)
- Application: IoT Narrowband Module
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: Fan-Out WLP
- Design Tool: Sonnet EM Suite v16
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Band-Pass Filter design targeting Band 26 (850 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1080.1 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       211.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.3 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 10.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 40.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 29.0 dB
Q Factor:               5810
Temperature Coefficient:-25.6 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.1 x 1.4 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   3
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Sonnet EM Suite v16 and load the Band-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1080.1 MHz, BW 211.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.3 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Fan-Out WLP).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 3240 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.3 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 10.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 316 MHz offset >= 40.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 3.5 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +33 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 90%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-06-02
Devices Tested:         93
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.05 dB
Return Loss (meas):     11.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       42.8 dB
Isolation (meas):       33.9 dB
Q Factor (meas):        5810
Group Delay Variation:  5.5 ns
Power Handling:         +30 dBm
Die Yield:              81.4%

Result Classification:  PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Band-Pass Filter design demonstrated excellent performance for Band 26 (850 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Design passed all acceptance criteria.
